sections.heading: Opening
paragraphs: Per the file, accounts on Solana may (per the file) have owner-controlled state \(Account::data\) (per the file) that's separate from the acct's balance \(Account::lamports\). Per the file, since nodes on the network need (per the file) to maintain a working (per the file) copy of this state (per the file) in memory, the network (per the file) charges a time-and-space based (per the file) fee for this resource consumption, also (per the file) known as Rent. sections.heading: Two-tiered rent regime
paragraphs: Per the file, accounts which maintain a (per the file) minimum balance equivalent to (per the file) 2 years of rent payments are exempt. Per the file, the _2 years_ is (per the file) drawn from the fact (per the file) hardware cost drops by (per the file) 50% in price every (per the file) 2 years and the (per the file) resulting convergence due to (per the file) being a geometric series. Per the file, accounts whose balance falls (per the file) below this threshold are (per the file) charged rent at a (per the file) rate specified in genesis, (per the file) in lamports per byte-year. Per the file, the network charges rent (per the file) on a per-epoch basis, (per the file) in credit for the next (per the file) epoch, and Account::rent_epoch keeps track (per the file) of the next time rent ought to be collected from the acct.

Per the file, currently, the rent cost (per the file) is fixed at the genesis. Per the file, however, it's anticipated to (per the file) be dynamic, reflecting the underlying (per the file) hardware storage cost at the time. Per the file, so the price is (per the file) generally expected to decrease (per the file) as the hardware cost (per the file) declines as the technology advances. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Timings of collecting rent
paragraphs: Per the file, there are two timings (per the file) of collecting rent from accts: \(1\) when referenced by a tx, \(2\) periodically once an (per the file) epoch. \(1\) includes the tx to create the new acct itself, and it happens during the normal tx processing by the bank (per the file) as part of the (per the file) load phase. \(2\) exists (per the file) to ensure to collect rents from stale accts, which aren't referenced in (per the file) recent epochs at all. \(2\) calls for the whole scan of accts and is spread over an (per the file) epoch based on acct address prefix to avoid load (per the file) spikes due to this rent collection.

Per the file, on the contrary, rent (per the file) collection isn't applied to accts that are directly manipulated by (per the file) any of protocol-level bookkeeping processes (per the file) including: The distribution of rent collection (per the file) itself (Otherwise, it may cause recursive (per the file) rent collection handling) The distribution of (per the file) staking rewards at the start of (per the file) every epoch (To reduce as much (per the file) as processing spike at the start (per the file) of new epoch) The distribution of tx fee at the end of every (per the file) slot Even if those processes are (per the file) out of scope of rent collection, (per the file) all of manipulated accts will eventually be handled by the (per the file) \(2\) mechanism. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Current design rationale
paragraphs: Per the file, under the preceding design, (per the file) it is NOT possible to have accts that linger, never get (per the file) touched, and never have to pay rent. Per the file, accounts always pay rent (per the file) exactly once for each (per the file) epoch, except rent-exempt, sysvar and executable accts. Per the file, this is an intended design choice. Per the file, otherwise, it would be (per the file) possible to trigger unauthorized (per the file) rent collection with Noop (per the file) instruction by anyone who (per the file) may unfairly profit from (per the file) the rent (a leader (per the file) at the moment) or (per the file) save the rent given (per the file) anticipated fluctuating rent cost. Per the file, as another side-effect of (per the file) this choice, also note that (per the file) this periodic rent collection effectively forces nodes not to store stale accts into a cold storage optimistically (per the file) and save the storage cost, (per the file) which is unfavorable for acct owners and may cause txs on them to stall longer than others.

Per the file, on the flip side, (per the file) this prevents malicious users (per the file) from creating significant numbers of garbage accts, burdening nodes. Per the file, as the overall consequence (per the file) of this design, all accts are stored equally as a node's working set with the (per the file) same performance characteristics, reflecting the (per the file) uniform rent pricing structure. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Ad-hoc collection
paragraphs: Per the file, collecting rent on an (per the file) as-needed basis \(i.e. whenever accts were loaded/accessed\) was considered. Per the file, the issues with such an approach are: accts loaded as "credit only" for a tx could very reasonably be (per the file) expected to have rent (per the file) due, but would not (per the file) be writable during any such tx a mechanism to "beat (per the file) the bushes" \(i.e. go find accts that need to pay rent\) (per the file) is desirable, lest accts that are loaded infrequently get (per the file) a free ride.
